messages:
Hannah: Emergency home office fashion show 1: router is currently balanced on an empty pizza box because my desk drawer jammed and the cat hid the screwdriver. Photo: https://images.redwood.example/hannah-pizza-router.jpg :pizza: :cat:

Leo: omg the aesthetic :joy: Does it actually work though?

Hannah: Works... ish. Video call last night had micro-freezes. Thinking about duct-taping it to a cutting board as a temp mount. Any better macgyver ideas?

Priya: First step: quick ping while you see the freeze to check jitter. Example I use:

Priya: ```
$ ping -c 5 1.1.1.1
PING 1.1.1.1 (1.1.1.1): 56 data bytes
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=1 ttl=57 time=11.2 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=2 ttl=57 time=104.9 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=3 ttl=57 time=10.8 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=4 ttl=57 time=12.0 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=5 ttl=57 time=11.1 ms
--- 1.1.1.1 ping statistics ---
5 packets transmitted, 5 packets received, 0% packet loss
round-trip min/avg/max = 10.8/30.0/104.9 ms
```

Tooling Bot: network-monitor: observed hannah-laptop spike at 2395004405; peak RTT 105ms, 2 retransmits in last 15m. Suggested: raise AP height, try 5GHz, or temporarily tether to phone during calls.

Omar: Cutting board + velcro is my go-to. If you're renting, velcro allows easy removal. Also try flipping the router orientation 10cm can help with antenna pattern.

Leo: Alternative stupid hack: hang it from a clothes hanger over the top of the desk so it's airborne and out of kitty reach. Works until gravity or the cat conspires. GIFs of catastrophes encouraged.

Hannah: Poll: react with :scissors: for "velcro cutting board", :zap: for "phone tether", :zap: for both? (ok that was bogus) :grin:

Priya: If the ping shows high jitter but low packet loss (like the example), it's interference. If you see dropped packets, look at the ISP side or modem. Also check for firmware updates.

Hannah: Ordered a small shelf clamp and some velcro. Will report back with a victory photo if the pizza box retires gracefully. Also accepted name suggestions for the router1 — current frontrunner: "Slice-Fi". :pizza::wifi:

Tooling Bot: network-monitor: hannah-laptop events cleared at 2395004568; no retransmits in last 10m after device raised. Marking resolved.

Hannah: Update: shelf clamp arrived, router elevated, cat confused but quiet. No dropouts during 60m meeting. Victory selfie: https://images.redwood.example/hannah-router-victory.jpg :tada:
